key_findings.finding: The CSF pattern (72 cells/mm3 with 75% lymphocytes, protein 50 mg/dL, normal glucose 70 mg/dL) is most consistent with acute viral/aseptic meningitis: typical viral meningitis has lymphocytic pleocytosis, modest protein elevation (about 20–80 mg/dL), and normal glucose; an enteroviral meningitis series specifically describes this profile.

Among the listed causes, enterovirus is the best fit because acute febrile meningitis with headache, photophobia, neck discomfort, a fine erythematous/exanthematous rash, lymphocytic CSF, modest protein elevation, and preserved glucose is characteristic; the available literature identifies non-polio enteroviruses as major causes of viral meningitis.

Tuberculous, cryptococcal/fungal, and bacterial meningitis are less likely because they more often produce substantially higher protein and/or low CSF glucose; viral encephalitis is less likely without altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic findings. LCMV is possible but rare, while mumps would generally require supportive exposure/parotitis or vaccination-context clues that are not provided.
